info.bio:
Aerosmith es una legendaria banda de rock formada en Estados Unidos. Fue creada a principios de los 70 por Steven Tyler (voz, teclado y armónica), Joe Perry (guitarra y coros), Brad Whitford (guitarra), Tom Hamilton (bajo) y Joey Kramer (batería).

La banda empezó a formarse cuando Steven Tyler formó "The Strangers", en 1964, en Sunapee, un pequeño pueblo de New Hampshire, donde tocaba la batería. Poco después, el nombre del grupo pasó a ser "Chain Reaction".

scenes.name: Hip hop neoyorquino
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Con la música negra popular muerta estéticamente, el alma del pueblo pasó al underground: un funk ruidoso, áspero y tenso, demasiado desesperado para la radio negra. Los breaks de DJ Kool Herc en las fiestas de barrio del Bronx, Jazzy Jay, Afrika Bambaataa, DJ Hollywood, Grandmaster Flash y Eddie Cheeba convirtieron la mezcla de discos en arte: los chavales dejaron las bandas por dos platos, el scratch y los breaks repetidos, un collage posmoderno de toda la música grabada sobre un ritmo funky. Sylvia Robinson grabó en 1979 «Rapper’s Delight» de la Sugarhill Gang y fichó a Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, cuya «The Message» (1982), con Melle Mel, dio voz a los sin voz como no se oía desde «What’s Going On»; siguieron «White Lines» o «New York, New York». Las cajas de ritmos dieron un funk industrial y minimalista (el bombo 808, «Five Minutes of Funk» de Whodini), y Run-D.M.C. («It’s Like That», «Rock Box», «King of Rock», «Walk This Way» con Aerosmith en Raising Hell, 1986) asaltó la radio rock, seguidos por los Beastie Boys.

scenes.name: Hard rock americano: Aerosmith, Kiss y Alice Cooper
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: En Estados Unidos la crítica, que detesta a Black Sabbath y a Judas Priest, evita el término «heavy metal» y prefiere «hard rock», el formato radiofónico de moda en los setenta, donde caben grupos muy populares que no cumplen del todo el código: Aerosmith (1973) y Kiss (1974) son demasiado melódicos para ser heavy en esa década. Cuando el género se fragmente, el lite metal adoptará su estilo vocal melódico y sus armonías, y ambos acabarán dentro del metal ampliado. Alice Cooper, que compartía cartel con Black Sabbath, regala al heavy la estética visual de película de terror.
scenes.family: Raíces: blues rock, psicodelia y hard rock

scenes.name: La radio: del exilio a Z-Rock
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Durante su primera década el heavy casi no suena en la radio: la FM progresiva rechaza a Black Sabbath por cambiar «love» por «evil», el AOR de los consultores solo pone «Stairway to Heaven» y algo de AC/DC, y a los anunciantes no les interesan los chicos de quince a dieciocho años. Weinstein ve ventajas en ese exilio: obliga a las bandas a girar sin parar (Aerosmith, Blue Öyster Cult y Ted Nugent, más de cuarenta semanas al año), las une a su público, las libra de los códigos radiofónicos (canciones de ocho minutos como «War Pigs», solos largos, el disco y no el single como unidad) y explica la abundancia de discos en directo. En los ochenta llegan los programas de metal en las radios universitarias (WSOU de Seton Hall se pasa entera al metal), el informe metal de CMJ y su Metal Marathon, y en la radio comercial el formato por satélite Z-Rock desde Dallas, que relega el thrash a su «Headbanger’s Heaven» nocturno. En Gran Bretaña, el único refugio es el «Friday Night Rock Show» de la BBC con Tommy Vance. Cuando la radio comercial acepta el metal es a través de MTV y de las power ballads, y exige productores de éxitos y solos recortados; aun así Metallica vende un millón de …And Justice for All sin apenas sonar.

scenes.name: Heavy metal de los setenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: «Born To Be Wild» de Steppenwolf acuña la expresión «heavy metal», que pasa a designar en EE UU el hard rock. Blue Oyster Cult definen el nuevo género (satanismo y serie B envueltos en riffs crudos); Aerosmith lo enlazan con el rhythm'n'blues depravado de Stones y Stooges; Kiss abrazan todos los estereotipos; AC/DC, las tripas del rock'n'roll (Back In Black); Journey y Boston, arquetipos del pop-metal; Rush reinventan el power-trio.

podcast.title: Awful Concert Sound (1978)
podcast.body: The concert in Winnipeg Arena on August 30, 1978, featured Aerosmith as the headliner and ACDC as the opener. The sound was extremely poor, described as a "blare of distortion" for over two and a half hours, making it impossible to recognize any of Aerosmith's songs. "People around me were going, are they playing Walk This Way or is that Walk in the Dog? I can't tell."

xref.title: Murder at Chelsea Hotel (October 12, 1978)
xref.body: Nancy Spungen, girlfriend of Sid Vicious, was found dead from a single stab wound to her stomach in room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel in New York on October 12, 1978. Nancy had a troubled life, diagnosed with schizophrenia at 15 and supporting herself through prostitution from age 17 before becoming a groupie to bands like The Ramones, New York Dolls, and Aerosmith. She became inseparable from Sid Vicious for 19 months, and they both were heroin and Tuinal addicts. On the night of October 11, 1978, several people visited their room, and Sid allegedly took up to 52 Tuinal tablets, completely incapacitating him. At around 2:30 am on October 12th, Nancy asked Rockets Redglare, their drug connection and Sid's bodyguard, for Dilaudid. Later, around 7:30 am, female moans were heard, and at 10 am, Sid called the front desk. Nancy was found stabbed and bleeding to death, in a weird angle under the bathroom sink. Sid initially confessed but was likely too incapacitated. The theory later emerged that Rockets Redglare, who died in 2007, was the murderer, allegedly stabbing Nancy with Sid's Bowie knife during an argument over stolen cash, a confession he reportedly made while drinking at CBGB. "Nancy Spungin, girlfriend of ex-sex Bristol Sidvicious, at the Chelsea Hotel on October 12, 1978."

xref.title: Derek Whibley's Recovery & Return to Music (2014)
xref.body: After his severe health crisis in May 2014, Derek Whibley embarked on a rigorous recovery, including daily physical therapy to regain his ability to walk and play guitar. By November 2014, he began writing music again and felt physically better. To reintegrate into the music world, he started attending concerts, including shows by Aerosmith and Fleetwood Mac, as he was unable to perform himself at the time. "I would say by November of 2014, I was starting to write music again and felt like I could kind of walk around, okay, and it was getting better."

In high school, he discovered punk rock, which was the prevalent live music scene in Santa Barbara and offered a more accessible social outlet compared to larger rock shows. "It wasn't until high school that I really got turned on to punk rock. And it was just like, because that was, you know, if you wanted to go to a show, there was no big rock show in Santa Barbara."

xref.title: Inspiration from 80s Music Videos
xref.body: Tadges-Krischlo's passion for music videos stemmed from watching influential artists like Madonna, Peter Gabriel, Phil Collins, Michael Jackson, and Aerosmith in the 1980s. He was fascinated by the storytelling, dancing, and style, which fueled his desire to enter the art form. "I came up, I came up in the 80s era where that's what made me fall in love with music videos, right? I was watching music videos by like Madonna and Peter Gabriel and like Phil Collins and Michael Jackson and Eros Smith. And I was always fascinated by music videos and the storytelling and the dancing and the style and all that stuff. And that's what got that's what made us fall in love with the art."

xref.title: Major Label Debut Scrutiny
xref.body: Their move to DGC shocked and horrified some indie fans who feared they had "sold out" to the establishment, particularly as DGC was also the label for artists like Cher and Aerosmith. However, their major label debut, "Goo," proved to be as noisy and non-mainstream as their earlier work. "And when it came out, it was scrutinized by the faithful for any sign that Sonic Youth had been tamed by the establishment."

xref.title: Plane's Prior Rejection by Aerosmith
xref.body: The Convair 240 offered to Leonard Skinnerd had previously been offered to Aerosmith earlier that same year. Aerosmith's manager, Peter Rudge (who also managed Skinnerd), was aware that Aerosmith had rejected the plane due to its poor condition and freaked out by its state. "The Conver, which by the way had been offered to Erosmith earlier that year. But they were so freaked out by the plane's poor condition, they said, thanks, but no thanks."

xref.title: Tour with Stone Temple Pilots
xref.body: Stone Temple Pilots opted to tour with the Butthole Surfers in June and July of 1993, turning down an offer to open for Aerosmith due to genre differences. It was during this tour that their singer, Gibby Haynes, allegedly introduced Scott Weiland to heroin. "So they turned that opportunity down in favor of a tour with, wait for it, the Butthole Surfers."
